harness_gate.run.description: One harness-gate run, at the end of every exit path that ran checks, interrupted runs included (interrupted=true, ok=false). at = run start, duration_s = run wall, head = the gated HEAD. checks = the run's declared checks; failed = the failed ones among those that finished. Emitter: DND-1474.

harness_gate.check.description: One finished check inside a harness-gate run. at = check start, duration_s = its wall_s. Emitter: DND-1474.

gate.run.description: One run of a repo's declared gate other than ai/bin/harness-gate (which writes harness_gate.run itself), written by test-slot after the command it held exits. A declared gate is the first ai/lib/integration-receipt.sh IR_DECLARED_GATES path that is a blob on the caller's HEAD, and the command (wrappers and interpreter skipped) must be that file in the caller's work tree, or the caller names it in ATHENA_TEST_SLOT_GATE_RUN (integration-gate does for its own `bash -c` gate run; test-slot checks the claim the same way and removes it from the command's environment). A gate run outside test-slot writes none. at = the command's start, duration_s = its wall, head = the caller's HEAD when it started. gate = the IR_DECLARED_GATES entry (never argv); exit = the command's exit code; ok = exit was 0; interrupted = INT/TERM/HUP reached test-slot while the command ran; slot_wait_s = the queue wait before it (0 for a nested run inside a held slot). None when the command never ran (a wait timeout, an orphaned or signalled waiter). Emitter: DND-1530.

test_slot.wait.description: test-slot's queue wait, after the slot is acquired (outcome=ran) or the wait times out (outcome=timeout) and before CMD runs. at = wait start, duration_s = the wait. A nested run already inside a slot waits for nothing and emits none. The run's --label is not an attr: it is caller free text (a work ticket id, a tree or command name), which Privacy keeps out. Emitter: DND-1474.

critic.round.description: One critic-review round, when its verdict receipt is written. at = started_at, duration_s = the receipt's duration_s, head = the judged sha. A carried PASS with no judge run has no started_at: a point event at the receipt's at. Emitter: DND-1474.

integration_gate.run.description: Exactly one per integration-gate invocation, on every exit path after its argv parse (the outer run emits; the run it re-executes inside test-slot reports facts to it). at = start, duration_s = wall (slot wait included), head = the head it judged (after --rebase, the rebased head). outcome = ok|red|refused|no_critic_pass|held|receipt_error|not_run|interrupted|other, keyed on exit_code. base = the target sha it contained, absent when the target never resolved. Emitter: DND-1475.

merge.lock_wait.description: Time blocked waiting for a merge lock (locked-merge, flock -w). at = wait start, duration_s = the wait, head = the gated head, unit from the PR head branch. lock = default|explicit (whether --lock was given; never the path), outcome = acquired|timeout. The custom ff push takes its lock by hand and emits none until DND-1370 gives it a tool. Emitter: DND-1475.

merge.landed.description: A landing on the default branch, a point event: a merge locked-merge confirmed (via=pr; at = confirmation, head = the gated PR head, unit from the PR head branch, before = the base, after = the merge commit) or a gh-athena push that moved the remote default branch (via=push; at = after the push, head = after, before absent when it could not be read). Emitter: DND-1475.

ticket.dispatched.description: A ticket moved to In Progress (or backfilled) by mark-in-progress, after its Notion write returned; never on a refusal, a dry run or a run that wrote nothing. at = the dispatch instant (--at, else now), a point event; head = the caller cwd HEAD, not the work. unit = the ticket ref (explicit). first_dispatch = this write set the stamp. Emitter: DND-1476.

mission.status.description: One per mission of a fleet-report admiral-scope report, written locally after the missions file is accepted and before the POST (not on --dry-run). Each report lists the whole scope, so an unchanged mission repeats: a reader takes the first event per (unit, status). A ticket_ref outside the ref grammar gets none. at = the write time, a point event; head = the caller cwd HEAD, not the work. unit = the mission ticket_ref (explicit). Emitter: DND-1476.

telemetry.probe.description: A by-hand or test probe of the writer itself (telemetry-emit --event telemetry.probe). Never a phase anchor: readers that compute phases ignore it.
